react_result.final_narrative_text: Differential metabolomics between control and treatment groups reveals a highly coordinated perturbation of tryptophan metabolism. Ten metabolites were significantly altered; nine resolved across KEGG, ChEBI, HMDB, and LIPIDMAPS namespaces. Cross-paradigm pathway analysis returned tryptophan metabolism as the unambiguous winner across all four active methods: RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 5.6e-18, 7 hits out of 54 pathway members, fold enrichment 778), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p=1.59e-08, 6 hits out of 41), mummichog m/z-direct network (p=0.0025, 17 of 18 pathway members overlapping), and WikiPathways ORA (FDR 1.7e-14). The driver metabolites span three canonical branches of the pathway: the serotonin-melatonin axis (tryptophan → tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin, with indoleacetaldehyde as the aromatic aldehyde intermediate), and the kynurenine-NAD+ shunt (tryptophan → N-formylkynurenine → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid). Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (Reactome R-HSA-209931) is the focused sub-pathway capturing the neurotransmitter output arm, confirmed by RaMP (FDR 3.4e-08, 3 of 15 members). A secondary, methodologically distinct signal from mummichog identified Arginine and Proline Metabolism (p=0.031) with near-complete pathway coverage (6 of 6 members hit), driven by 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid and pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid — proline-cycle intermediates that are downstream of ornithine and upstream of glutamate semialdehyde. Valine biosynthesis (MetaboAnalystR p=0.044) appears as a minor signal driven solely by L-valine, consistent with branched-chain amino acid cross-talk. The convergence of ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR), m/z-direct network (mummichog), and KEGG-specific hits on tryptophan metabolism across six distinct pathway databases, with fold enrichments ranging from 581 to 1637, represents a robust multi-paradigm consensus. The biological interpretation is a treatment-induced re-routing of tryptophan flux away from the serotonin-melatonin axis and toward the kynurenine-NAD+ branch, with simultaneous perturbation of the proline-cycle derived pyrroline pool — a pattern consistent with inflammatory or neuroactive shift.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary enrichment methods converge on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380) as the dominant affected pathway with FDR = 5.56e-18 (RaMP ORA, multi-DB), p = 1.59e-08 (MetaboAnalystR PSEA, KEGG), and p = 0.000672 (Mummichog m/z-direct). Seven input metabolites map to this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, and tryptamine. WikiPathways Tryptophan metabolism (WP:WP465) achieves FDR = 1.73e-14 and Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210) achieves FDR = 1.46e-10, confirming the kynurenine branch of the pathway is active alongside the serotonin-melatonin branch. Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) is enriched at FDR = 3.38e-08. Arginine and proline metabolism (MUMM, p = 0.0268) captures 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid and pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid, representing the interface between proline synthesis and tryptophan-linked glutamate metabolism. L-valine appears in glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism and the urea cycle, but these hits are weaker and not replicated across paradigms.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary enrichment methods converge on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380) as the dominant affected pathway with FDR = 5.56e-18 (RaMP ORA, multi-DB), p = 1.59e-08 (MetaboAnalystR PSEA, KEGG), and p = 0.000672 (Mummichog m/z-direct). Seven input metabolites map to this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, and tryptamine. WikiPathways Tryptophan metabolism (WP:WP465) achieves FDR = 1.73e-14 and Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210) achieves FDR = 1.46e-10, confirming the kynurenine branch of the pathway is active alongside the serotonin-melatonin branch. Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) is enriched at FDR = 3.38e-08. Arginine and proline metabolism (MUMM, p = 0.0268) captures 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid and pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid, representing the interface between proline synthesis and tryptophan-linked glutamate metabolism. L-valine appears in glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism and the urea cycle, but these hits are weaker and not replicated across paradigms.
